title: Closed-Loop Validity Tests for Offline-Accurate Visuomotor Policies
current_belief: Embodied policies are often promoted using offline prediction or imitation metrics that may not reveal feedback-loop instability.
proposed_challenge: Test whether offline accuracy preserves the ordering of policies once their predictions alter future observations and actions.
scientific_question: When does offline visuomotor accuracy cease to predict closed-loop task success under observation and actuation perturbations?
falsifiable_claim: Across at least three perturbation families, offline error ranking will disagree with closed-loop success ranking for at least 25% of policy pairs, while a stability-aware score will reduce that discordance by at least 30%.
why_now: The supplied literature reports a neural estimator that performs extremely well offline yet must be assessed inside a feedback loop, while current robotics calls emphasize reliable embodied learning.
reasoning_summary: This transfers a documented offline-versus-loop distinction into robot policy evaluation and asks for an identification boundary rather than another accuracy benchmark.
cheap_falsifier: Replay two public control policies in simulation with one-step observation delay; abandon the idea if offline and closed-loop rankings remain identical across seeds and delay levels.
main_risk: Ranking reversals may be specific to unstable controllers rather than general to learned visuomotor policies.
proposed_data_source: Public simulated manipulation or locomotion rollouts with logged observations, actions, and perturbation sweeps
target_variable: closed-loop success rank discordance

title: Uncertainty-Triggered Active Perception for Tabletop Planning
current_belief: Uncertainty-aware symbolic planners can request information-gathering actions, but a fixed confidence threshold may not remain calibrated across scene difficulty or sensor shift.
proposed_challenge: Replace a global trigger threshold with a risk-calibrated decision rule that accounts for predicate uncertainty and the cost of an extra observation.
scientific_question: Can cost-aware calibration choose active-perception actions more reliably than a fixed confidence threshold in cluttered manipulation?
falsifiable_claim: At matched task success, a cost-aware trigger will reduce unnecessary information-gathering actions by at least 15% without increasing unsafe plan execution by more than 1 percentage point.
why_now: The supplied neuro-symbolic planning work exposes calibrated predicate confidence and explicit look-closer actions, creating a direct test bed for decision calibration.
reasoning_summary: The opportunity lies in connecting calibrated perception to the downstream value of information rather than treating confidence as an isolated score.
expected_contribution_type: decision rule and controlled benchmark study
cheap_falsifier: Sweep fixed and cost-aware thresholds on existing simulated RGB-D scenes; stop if the Pareto frontiers for success and sensing cost overlap within bootstrap uncertainty.
main_risk: Results may depend on an arbitrary cost model for information-gathering actions.
proposed_data_source: PyBullet tabletop scenes with injected occlusion, depth noise, and action costs
target_variable: unsafe-execution rate at matched sensing cost

title: Action-Sufficient State Compression for Robot Control
current_belief: Predictive representations retain distinctions needed to forecast futures, although a controller may only need distinctions that change the set of acceptable actions.
proposed_challenge: Measure whether action-sufficient abstractions can be smaller than predictive-state representations without sacrificing safe task completion.
scientific_question: How much can an embodied agent compress its latent state when the preservation target is acceptable action rather than full future prediction?
falsifiable_claim: On finite-state partially observed control tasks, an action-sufficient code will use at least 20% fewer discrete states than a prediction-sufficient code while keeping unacceptable-action probability within 1 percentage point.
why_now: A supplied formal result distinguishes predictive state from viable action, while robotics venues are actively soliciting work on embodied reasoning and control.
reasoning_summary: This converts a static action-sufficiency distinction into a measurable representation-learning hypothesis while keeping recursive updateability as an explicit limitation.
cheap_falsifier: Enumerate belief states and acceptable-action sets in small POMDPs; reject the premise if minimum action and predictive partitions have equal size across the suite.
main_risk: Static action sufficiency may fail to produce a recursively updateable controller state.
proposed_data_source: Small tabular POMDPs plus a simulated partially observed manipulation task
target_variable: minimum latent code size at a fixed action-risk tolerance

title: Scale-Aware Abstention for Edge Robot Planners
current_belief: Small language models deployed on edge devices need abstention, but inexpensive confidence signals can degrade differently as model scale changes.
proposed_challenge: Test whether confidence calibrators chosen at one language-model scale remain valid when the model is embedded in a robot planning stack at another scale.
scientific_question: Which confidence signal best preserves selective planning risk across sub-7B models used for embodied instruction following?
falsifiable_claim: Sampling-consistency calibration will improve failure AUROC by at least 0.05 over token-probability calibration on models at or below 1B parameters, at a compute overhead below two additional plan samples per accepted action on average.
why_now: The supplied cross-scale calibration study identifies scale-dependent confidence degradation, and edge robotics creates a consequential deployment setting for that claim.
reasoning_summary: The candidate tests whether a language-only calibration result survives contact with embodied action risk and strict compute budgets.
cheap_falsifier: Run two small open-weight models on a simulator instruction set; drop the idea if all confidence signals have indistinguishable selective-risk curves.
main_risk: Planning failures may be dominated by perception or control rather than language-model uncertainty.
proposed_data_source: Simulated household instruction-following episodes with plan validity labels
target_variable: selective task-failure risk versus inference cost

title: Does Low-Rank Test-Time Adaptation Destabilize Robot Feedback Loops?
current_belief: Low-rank test-time adaptation can reduce update cost under domain shift, but adaptation is usually evaluated on prediction performance rather than feedback-loop stability.
proposed_challenge: Insert low-rank and full-parameter test-time adaptation into the same visual-control loop and compare stability under matched update budgets.
scientific_question: Can low-rank test-time adaptation improve shifted visual perception without inducing closed-loop oscillation or policy drift?
falsifiable_claim: Under at least two visual shifts, low-rank adaptation will recover at least 80% of the task-success gain of full adaptation while producing at least 25% fewer instability events.
why_now: The supplied literature combines an efficient LoRA-TTA proposal with direct evidence that offline estimator quality is insufficient for closed-loop safety.
reasoning_summary: Efficiency claims become scientifically stronger if adaptation is evaluated as part of a dynamical system rather than as an isolated predictor.
cheap_falsifier: Apply low-rank updates to a visual line-following controller under color shift; stop if adaptation never changes loop dynamics relative to the frozen model.
main_risk: Observed instability may arise from an aggressive optimizer rather than the low-rank parameterization.
proposed_data_source: Vision-based control simulators with controlled appearance shifts and high-frequency trajectory logs
target_variable: instability-event rate under test-time adaptation

title: Attention-Heatmap Drift as an Early Warning for Embodied Transfer Failure
current_belief: Vision-language adaptation can improve in-domain accuracy while changing attention patterns and degrading unseen transfer, but the predictive value of attention drift for control is unresolved.
proposed_challenge: Evaluate attention drift as a prospective warning signal rather than a post-hoc visualization.
scientific_question: Does attention-heatmap drift predict out-of-domain robot policy failure earlier than validation accuracy?
falsifiable_claim: Across adaptation checkpoints, attention-drift features will predict held-out control failure with AUROC at least 0.10 higher than in-domain validation accuracy alone.
why_now: A supplied controlled comparison measures attention drift under full and low-rank adaptation, while multimodal fine-tuning work highlights heterogeneous component failure modes.
reasoning_summary: The key gap is identification: whether representation drift contains actionable pre-deployment information about embodied transfer loss.
cheap_falsifier: Adapt one vision-language encoder on a small manipulation dataset and correlate heatmap drift with held-out simulator success; abandon if the correlation is near zero with wide uncertainty.
main_risk: Attention maps may be unstable or non-causal explanations of policy behavior.
proposed_data_source: Checkpointed vision-language robot policies evaluated on held-out object, texture, and viewpoint splits
target_variable: AUROC for predicting held-out policy failure

title: Dynamic Rank Allocation for Vision-Language Robot Adaptation
current_belief: A fixed low-rank budget treats every layer and task phase alike even though embodied adaptation demands may be sparse and task dependent.
proposed_challenge: Learn and prune rank components under a joint objective for task success, transfer retention, and deployment memory.
scientific_question: Can rank-gated low-rank adaptation discover a smaller and more transferable parameter update for vision-language robot policies than fixed-rank LoRA?
falsifiable_claim: Rank-gated adaptation will match fixed-rank LoRA within 1 percentage point of in-domain success while reducing retained adapter parameters by at least 30% and improving held-out success by at least 3 points.
why_now: The supplied rank-gated LoRA work and modality-aware adaptation survey jointly motivate sparse, locus-specific updates, but embodied policy transfer remains an open test.
reasoning_summary: This asks whether rank sparsity is a real property of embodied adaptation rather than merely a compression device.
cheap_falsifier: Train gated and fixed-rank adapters on one small vision-language control task; reject if gates remain dense and no parameter reduction is possible without loss.
main_risk: Gating gains may disappear after fair hyperparameter matching.
proposed_data_source: Public vision-language manipulation benchmark with object and scene generalization splits
target_variable: held-out task success per retained adapter parameter

title: Long-Tail Skill Metrics for Embodied Benchmarks
current_belief: Aggregate success can conceal severe failure on rare classes or skills, especially when evaluation distributions are imbalanced.
proposed_challenge: Replace one-number robot benchmark reporting with frequency-stratified success, worst-group risk, and uncertainty intervals.
scientific_question: How often do aggregate embodied-agent scores reverse model rankings once rare skills and objects receive explicit weight?
falsifiable_claim: On at least two embodied benchmarks, frequency-stratified evaluation will reverse at least one pairwise model ranking and reveal a worst-decile skill success rate at least 20 points below the aggregate score.
why_now: The supplied oracle-character study explicitly shows aggregate metrics concealing long-tailed defects, and a NeurIPS evaluations-and-datasets signal supports benchmark-focused work.
reasoning_summary: The cross-domain transfer is methodological: class-frequency diagnostics from recognition become skill-frequency diagnostics for embodied evaluation.
cheap_falsifier: Recompute frequency deciles from one benchmark's public episode logs; stop if skill frequencies are balanced and stratification changes neither conclusions nor rankings.
main_risk: Existing logs may not contain reliable skill or object-frequency annotations.
proposed_data_source: Public episode-level embodied benchmark results with task, object, and success metadata
target_variable: worst-decile skill success and ranking reversal count

title: Voice Lever or Judgment Lever? Role Prompts in Robot Decision Making
current_belief: Character prompts strongly affect phrasing on subjective tasks but may have little effect on factual verification; robot-agent role prompts could similarly alter explanations without changing decisions.
proposed_challenge: Separate linguistic style attribution from changes in action selection, factual scene judgments, and safety refusals.
scientific_question: Do role personas change an embodied agent's control judgments, or only the language used to explain them?
falsifiable_claim: Across at least four personas, style-attribution accuracy will change by at least 30 points while action-selection agreement changes by less than 5 points on fact-grounded tasks.
why_now: The supplied persona crossover reports task-conditioned effects, while language-supervised autonomous driving supplies an embodied reasoning chain where wording and action can be measured separately.
reasoning_summary: A controlled decomposition would prevent verbal differences from being mistaken for policy-level behavioral control.
cheap_falsifier: Apply four personas to a small driving-QA set and compare both lexical style and selected action; drop if neither output dimension changes.
main_risk: Prompted explanations may not be causally connected to the policy action head.
proposed_data_source: Driving or navigation scenarios with paired natural-language rationales and discrete action labels
target_variable: persona-induced action disagreement versus style shift

title: Delta-Encoded 4D Scene Memory for Long-Horizon Robots
current_belief: Dynamic Gaussian-splat representations can store temporal change compactly, but their usefulness as robot memory depends on preserving task-relevant changes over long horizons.
proposed_challenge: Evaluate per-frame delta encoding by downstream navigation and manipulation decisions rather than rendering quality alone.
scientific_question: What compression level can a delta-encoded 4D scene memory sustain before task-relevant temporal changes become unusable for embodied planning?
falsifiable_claim: A delta-encoded memory will reduce storage by at least 50% relative to independent-frame splats while keeping change-conditioned action success within 3 percentage points.
why_now: The supplied differential 4D Gaussian-splat work targets temporal scalability, and current vision and robotics calls create a natural venue for task-grounded evaluation.
reasoning_summary: The benchmark changes the unit of value from photorealistic replay to whether temporal memory supports the right action.
cheap_falsifier: Compress a short synthetic scene with moving obstacles and test collision-free planning; stop if storage savings are negligible or planning fails even without compression.
main_risk: Gaussian-splat rendering artifacts may confound the intended memory-capacity question.
proposed_data_source: Synthetic indoor dynamic scenes with ground-truth object trajectories and navigation queries
target_variable: task success as a function of bytes per temporal scene

title: Temporal Coherence Without Wave Erasure in Robot World Models
current_belief: Temporal smoothing improves coherent reconstruction but can erase small, fast surface changes that may matter for contact or locomotion.
proposed_challenge: Design a world-model objective that preserves high-frequency task cues while suppressing frame-wise reconstruction jitter.
scientific_question: Can frequency-aware temporal regularization preserve contact-relevant microdynamics better than uniform smoothing in monocular world models?
falsifiable_claim: Frequency-aware regularization will reduce temporal jitter by at least 20% while retaining at least 90% of ground-truth high-frequency energy and improving contact-timing error by at least 10%.
why_now: The supplied monocular fluid work explicitly identifies the tension between temporal coherence and fine-wave preservation.
reasoning_summary: This turns an image-reconstruction trade-off into a downstream dynamics question with measurable control consequences.
cheap_falsifier: Use procedurally generated waves with known spectra; reject if uniform smoothing already lies on the same jitter-versus-detail frontier.
main_risk: Synthetic wave spectra may not reflect task-relevant real-world dynamics.
proposed_data_source: Rendered monocular fluid and deformable-surface sequences with ground-truth geometry
target_variable: contact-timing error under controlled temporal smoothing

title: Viewpoint-Invariance Versus Temporal Consistency in Action-Centric Perception
current_belief: Embodied action detectors need both viewpoint invariance and temporal consistency, but optimizing one may suppress cues needed by the other.
proposed_challenge: Build a matched intervention matrix that independently strengthens viewpoint augmentation and temporal regularization.
scientific_question: Is there a measurable trade-off between viewpoint invariance and temporal boundary accuracy in robot action detection?
falsifiable_claim: Increasing viewpoint invariance will improve cross-view action AP by at least 5 points but worsen temporal boundary error by at least 10% unless the model uses separate spatial and temporal adaptation paths.
why_now: A supplied paper title directly targets both properties, while temporally coherent reconstruction work supplies a complementary mechanism for controlled testing.
reasoning_summary: The contribution would identify whether two commonly bundled desiderata are actually compatible under a fixed model budget.
cheap_falsifier: Run a 2x2 augmentation and temporal-loss grid on one multi-view action dataset; stop if both metrics improve monotonically with no interaction.
main_risk: The supplied action-detection record lacks an abstract, so the exact prior scope requires later literature verification.
proposed_data_source: Multi-view robot-action videos with frame-level temporal boundaries
target_variable: cross-view AP and temporal boundary error interaction

title: Calibrated Synthetic Vibration for Robot Fault Learning
current_belief: Text-conditioned diffusion can generate vibration signals with uncertainty estimates, but synthetic augmentation is useful only if uncertainty predicts downstream diagnostic value under domain shift.
proposed_challenge: Filter or weight generated robot vibration sequences using calibrated uncertainty before training a fault classifier.
scientific_question: Does uncertainty-filtered vibration synthesis improve low-label robot fault diagnosis under changes in load, speed, and sensor placement?
falsifiable_claim: With no more than 20 labeled target examples per fault, uncertainty-filtered augmentation will improve shifted-domain macro-F1 by at least 5 points over unfiltered synthetic augmentation.
why_now: The supplied U-T2V study connects calibrated generative uncertainty to predictive-maintenance augmentation, offering a direct cross-domain test on robotic hardware.
reasoning_summary: The study would test uncertainty as a selection mechanism, not merely report fidelity of generated signals.
cheap_falsifier: Train on one public bearing dataset with a held-out load condition; abandon if uncertainty is uncorrelated with synthetic-sample utility.
main_risk: Industrial bearing vibrations may not transfer to faults in articulated robots.
proposed_data_source: Public vibration datasets plus small motor or joint recordings under controlled faults
target_variable: shifted-domain fault macro-F1 per target label

title: Physical-Consistency Gates for Open-World Robot Alarms
current_belief: Closed-set recognition accuracy can coexist with high false-alarm rates on unknown nuisance events, and confidence thresholding alone may not eliminate the problem.
proposed_challenge: Combine learned confidence with a label-free physical-consistency test tailored to robot sensor dynamics.
scientific_question: Can physical-consistency gating reduce open-world robot false alarms without suppressing novel hazardous events?
falsifiable_claim: At 95% recall on known hazards, a physical-consistency gate will reduce false alarms on unseen nuisances by at least 30% relative to confidence-only conformal thresholding.
why_now: The supplied optical-fiber study reports a closed-set/open-world failure and proposes physical consistency as a corrective signal; embodied sensing offers a high-impact transfer setting.
reasoning_summary: This tests whether invariants from robot kinematics or sensor physics can reject unknown nuisances more robustly than model confidence.
cheap_falsifier: Inject impossible kinematic patterns and realistic nuisance signals into logged sensor traces; stop if the gate cannot separate them above chance.
main_risk: A rigid physics gate may reject real hazards that violate the assumed model.
proposed_data_source: Robot proprioceptive and force-torque logs with known events plus synthetically and physically generated nuisances
target_variable: open-world false-alarm rate at fixed hazard recall

title: Ranking Disagreement as Uncertainty in Language-Grounded Object Retrieval
current_belief: Embedding uncertainty may not reflect the reliability of the final ranked list used by an embodied agent.
proposed_challenge: Estimate uncertainty from disagreement between global-semantic and local-detail object rankings before committing to a grasp or navigation target.
scientific_question: Does cross-granularity ranking disagreement predict language-grounding failures better than embedding-space uncertainty?
falsifiable_claim: Cross-granularity disagreement will improve grounding-error AUROC by at least 0.07 over embedding variance and reduce wrong-object actions by at least 15% under selective abstention.
why_now: The supplied image-text retrieval work measures uncertainty directly in ranking space, which maps naturally to object selection in embodied tasks.
reasoning_summary: The candidate moves uncertainty estimation to the decision object that actually drives behavior: the candidate ranking.
cheap_falsifier: Evaluate global/local rank disagreement on a small referring-expression set; reject if incorrect targets show no higher disagreement than correct targets.
main_risk: Global and local rankers may share errors, making disagreement falsely reassuring.
proposed_data_source: Referring-expression grounding data augmented with clutter and attribute-confusable objects
target_variable: wrong-object action rate under selective grounding

title: Identity-Calibrated Forecasting for Social Robot Navigation
current_belief: Crowd trajectory models can combine identity-aware representations with post-hoc confidence calibration, but calibration must be tied to collision risk rather than trajectory error alone.
proposed_challenge: Evaluate whether persistent identity improves both uncertainty calibration and safe planning in dense social navigation.
scientific_question: Does identity-aware trajectory calibration reduce collision risk for social robots under re-identification errors and crowd occlusion?
falsifiable_claim: Identity-aware calibration will reduce collision rate by at least 20% at matched travel time when identity switches remain below 10%, but lose that advantage once switches exceed a measurable threshold.
why_now: The supplied crowd-forecasting record proposes identity-aware calibrated prediction, while robotics calls foreground real-world navigation and interaction.
reasoning_summary: The experiment identifies a failure boundary for identity-aware forecasting rather than assuming identity information is always beneficial.
cheap_falsifier: Inject controlled identity switches into recorded crowd tracks and compare risk calibration; stop if identity features never affect risk estimates or plans.
main_risk: Duplicate supplied literature records may represent one underlying study rather than independent evidence.
proposed_data_source: Public pedestrian trajectory datasets replayed in a robot navigation simulator
target_variable: collision rate versus identity-switch probability

title: Safe Diagnostic Actions Before Manipulation Commitment
current_belief: When hidden states require different safe actions, passive observation may be insufficient; limited diagnostic actions can improve decisions but consume time and may disturb the scene.
proposed_challenge: Learn when to inspect, probe, or reposition before committing to an irreversible manipulation action.
scientific_question: When does an active diagnostic action make a partially observed manipulation problem operationally recoverable before its rescue window closes?
falsifiable_claim: For tasks with disjoint acceptable actions across hidden states, one learned non-destructive diagnostic will reduce unacceptable actions by at least 25% whenever the induced observation total variation exceeds the decision threshold predicted by the supplied recoverability bound.
why_now: The supplied action-sufficiency work gives a formal diagnostic limit, and uncertainty-aware planning supplies concrete information-gathering actions.
reasoning_summary: This operationalizes a formal bound as a robotics experiment with explicit time, disturbance, and action-availability constraints.
cheap_falsifier: Construct a two-hidden-state simulator with one probe; reject if empirical selection error does not track observation separability.
main_risk: A diagnostic useful in simulation may be unavailable or unsafe on real hardware.
proposed_data_source: Partially observed tabletop tasks with hidden mass, friction, or attachment state
target_variable: unacceptable-action probability before deadline

title: Reportability Before Interpretability in Robot Latent Dynamics
current_belief: Named latent coefficients are not automatically interpretable; structural identifiability and practical recovery must be established before mechanistic claims are reported.
proposed_challenge: Audit which latent dynamics parameters can actually be recovered from standard robot observation and action logs.
scientific_question: Which parameters of a mechanistic robot world model are structurally identifiable and practically recoverable under the deployed observation policy?
falsifiable_claim: At least one semantically named parameter will show non-identifiability or rank recovery below 0.5 under the default logging policy, while an orthogonalized intervention will improve its recovery by at least 0.15 Spearman correlation.
why_now: The supplied identifiability study distinguishes semantic assignment from recoverability and demonstrates configuration-dependent reporting limits.
reasoning_summary: The candidate makes interpretability claims conditional on an explicit parameter-to-observation map and recovery experiment.
expected_contribution_type: identifiability audit and experimental design rule
cheap_falsifier: Run synthetic recovery on a two-parameter dynamics model; stop if all parameters are trivially identifiable and accurately recovered under passive logs.
main_risk: A simple simulator may overstate identifiability relative to a real robot.
proposed_data_source: Synthetic robot dynamics with known parameters plus matched logged trajectories
target_variable: parameter rank recovery under alternative observation policies

title: Hidden Recovery State in Repeated Robot Repair Tasks
current_belief: A system may appear recovered under the current task yet retain a hidden state that changes its response to a later perturbation.
proposed_challenge: Detect latent post-recovery state by re-challenging a robot after apparently successful adaptation or repair.
scientific_question: Can two robot policies with identical immediate recovery behavior be distinguished by their response to a standardized second perturbation?
falsifiable_claim: A re-challenge protocol will separate at least two post-recovery policy states whose initial task success differs by less than 2 points but whose second-perturbation recovery time differs by at least 20%.
why_now: The supplied planarian model motivates persistent hidden recovery state, while embodied learning needs protocols that go beyond immediate task restoration.
reasoning_summary: This is a cross-domain transfer of a hidden-state diagnostic, not a claim that biological regeneration and robot learning share a mechanism.
cheap_falsifier: Adapt two policies to one actuator perturbation, restore nominal conditions, then repeat the perturbation; reject if second responses contain no additional information.
main_risk: The effect may reduce to optimizer state rather than a scientifically interesting policy memory.
proposed_data_source: Simulated locomotion policies subjected to repeated actuator or morphology perturbations
target_variable: second-challenge recovery time conditional on first recovery success

title: Preparation-Time Corrections for Measuring Robot Micro-Learning
current_belief: Performance gains measured across brief rests can change sign when preparation time is included, so apparent offline learning may be a timing artifact.
proposed_challenge: Recompute short-horizon robot skill gains using both action-execution time and pre-action planning time.
scientific_question: Do reported micro-offline gains in iterative robot skill learning persist after accounting for action preparation latency?
falsifiable_claim: Including planning latency will change the sign or halve the magnitude of measured between-bout gains in at least one commonly used online adaptation setting.
why_now: Two supplied motor-learning papers disagree with common micro-offline interpretations and isolate preparation-time measurement as a plausible source of reversal.
reasoning_summary: The research gap is measurement validity: whether learning is inferred from a metric that omits part of the action cycle.
cheap_falsifier: Reanalyze one public adaptation log with and without pre-action latency; stop if estimates are identical within numerical tolerance.
main_risk: Human motor preparation may not map cleanly to machine planning latency.
proposed_data_source: Timestamped robot-learning episodes containing observation, planning-start, action-start, and action-end times
target_variable: between-bout performance gain with preparation-time correction

title: Evaluation-Trajectory Recycling Under Closed-Loop Shift
current_belief: Offline policy improvement can reuse evaluation trajectories, but recycled data may become misleading as the updated policy changes the visited state distribution.
proposed_challenge: Quantify when trajectory recycling remains valid and when closed-loop distribution shift breaks its advantage.
scientific_question: How much policy-induced state-distribution shift can evaluation-trajectory recycling tolerate before offline improvement becomes harmful?
falsifiable_claim: A divergence gate on recycled trajectories will prevent at least half of harmful updates while retaining at least 80% of beneficial updates across controlled traffic shifts.
why_now: The supplied eco-driving title proposes closed-loop offline improvement through trajectory recycling, and the offline-instability study warns that loop behavior can invalidate static evaluation.
reasoning_summary: The study targets an identification boundary for data reuse rather than assuming recycled evaluation data remain on-policy enough.
cheap_falsifier: Recycle trajectories in a toy signalized-intersection simulator while increasing behavior-policy divergence; reject if harmful updates never emerge.
main_risk: The relevant supplied paper has no abstract, so its exact algorithmic assumptions need later verification.
proposed_data_source: Signalized-intersection simulator with logged evaluation trajectories and controlled demand shifts
target_variable: rate of harmful policy updates versus trajectory divergence

title: Spatial-Uncertainty Stress Tests for Multi-Robot Offloading
current_belief: Task-offloading policies in digital-twin UAV networks can be brittle when spatial estimates differ from the deployed environment.
proposed_challenge: Evaluate offloading decisions under structured localization, channel-map, and mobility-model errors rather than average random noise.
scientific_question: Which forms of spatial uncertainty most strongly reverse task-offloading decisions in digital-twin-enabled robot teams?
falsifiable_claim: Correlated spatial bias will cause at least twice as many offloading decision reversals as equal-variance independent noise, and a robust policy will reduce deadline misses by at least 15% under that bias.
why_now: A supplied 2026 record directly identifies robust task offloading under spatial uncertainty, while robotics venues solicit multi-agent and networked systems work.
reasoning_summary: The candidate emphasizes structured perturbations and decision reversals, which are more diagnostic than mean latency alone.
cheap_falsifier: Simulate two UAVs and one edge server under independent versus correlated position errors; stop if decision reversals and deadline misses are unchanged.
main_risk: The offloading literature record lacks an abstract, limiting confidence about novelty until a later audit.
proposed_data_source: Digital-twin UAV-network simulator with controllable localization and channel-map errors
target_variable: deadline-miss rate under structured spatial uncertainty

title: Spectral Early Warning for Cascading Failures in Robot Teams
current_belief: Local perturbations can propagate through coupled systems, yet robot-team monitoring often focuses on per-agent failures rather than network-level stability.
proposed_challenge: Transfer multiscale spectral stability diagnostics from networked infrastructure to communication-coupled robot teams.
scientific_question: Can a spectral stability statistic predict cascade onset in multi-robot coordination before task-level performance collapses?
falsifiable_claim: A spectral statistic computed from interaction graphs will predict cascade onset at least five control steps earlier than aggregate task error with AUROC above 0.80 across two coupling topologies.
why_now: The supplied smart-grid work proposes an operator view of multiscale cascading failure, while multi-robot systems present analogous coupled perturbation pathways worth testing.
reasoning_summary: The transfer is a falsifiable systems hypothesis about coupled dynamics, not an assertion that power grids and robot teams are equivalent.
cheap_falsifier: Simulate consensus control with one degraded agent; reject if graph spectra provide no earlier signal than mean tracking error.
main_risk: Spectral changes may simply restate obvious communication-graph degradation.
proposed_data_source: Multi-agent formation and task-allocation simulations with injected sensor, actuator, and communication faults
target_variable: lead time and AUROC for cascade prediction

title: Separating Model Uncertainty from Ensemble Disagreement in Robot Perception
current_belief: Raw forecast disagreement can conflate disagreement between models with uncertainty within each model, leading to incorrect interpretations of risk.
proposed_challenge: Decompose ensemble dispersion for robot perception and test which component predicts downstream errors under shift.
scientific_question: Does within-model uncertainty or between-model disagreement better identify unsafe robot perception decisions under domain shift?
falsifiable_claim: After decomposition, within-model uncertainty will explain more than 60% of raw ensemble dispersion and outperform between-model disagreement by at least 0.05 AUROC for unsafe-decision prediction.
why_now: The supplied finance study shows that raw machine disagreement can mostly reflect model uncertainty, while QUAD separately integrates uncertainty, domain risk, and disagreement.
reasoning_summary: The candidate tests whether a widely used ensemble signal has the interpretation practitioners assign to it.
cheap_falsifier: Use a small deep ensemble on shifted image classification and estimate both components; stop if the decomposition is unidentifiable or components are perfectly collinear.
main_risk: The Bayesian decomposition from investor forecasts may require assumptions that do not hold for neural ensembles.
proposed_data_source: Ensembles of robot perception models evaluated on controlled visual and sensor shifts
target_variable: unsafe-decision AUROC by uncertainty component

title: Competence-Confidence Calibration in Human-Robot Shared Control
current_belief: Human self-confidence can diverge from objective competence, and shared-control systems that trust confidence reports may allocate autonomy poorly.
proposed_challenge: Use observed competence-confidence mismatch to adapt authority allocation during training and operation.
scientific_question: Does calibration-aware shared control outperform confidence-only authority allocation for novice operators?
falsifiable_claim: Calibration-aware allocation will reduce critical task errors by at least 15% relative to confidence-only allocation without increasing completion time by more than 10%.
why_now: The supplied nursing study foregrounds competence-confidence mismatch as a safety concern, offering a human-factors bridge to robot teleoperation.
reasoning_summary: The study turns a human calibration measurement into a concrete autonomy-allocation rule with safety and efficiency outcomes.
cheap_falsifier: Run a small simulated teleoperation study using historical competence plus trial-level confidence; reject if mismatch does not predict errors.
main_risk: The supplied confidence evidence is from a small cross-sectional educational setting and may not generalize to teleoperation.
proposed_data_source: Controlled novice teleoperation sessions with confidence ratings and objective task scores
target_variable: critical error rate under adaptive authority allocation

title: Difficulty-Controlled Language Curricula for Robot Skills
current_belief: Generated tasks can be assigned nominal difficulty levels, but semantic drift increases when generation moves into unfamiliar domains.
proposed_challenge: Generate robot-language tasks with controlled compositional difficulty and independently verify both semantics and embodied solvability.
scientific_question: Can a generator-critic curriculum control embodied task difficulty without increasing semantic drift across new robot domains?
falsifiable_claim: A critic-filtered curriculum will keep intended-versus-measured difficulty correlation above 0.70 and reduce semantic-invalidity rate by at least 30% relative to unfiltered generation on a held-out domain.
why_now: The supplied test-generation work reports controlled difficulty and a 12-18% unfamiliar-domain quality drop, while language supervision is entering end-to-end embodied systems.
reasoning_summary: The key advance would be validating difficulty against actual agent performance and semantic executability, not taxonomy labels alone.
cheap_falsifier: Generate 100 simulator instructions across three nominal levels and test monotonicity against a baseline agent; stop if measured success is unrelated to intended difficulty.
main_risk: Agent-specific competence may confound intrinsic task difficulty.
proposed_data_source: Procedurally generated household manipulation tasks with executable goal predicates
target_variable: correlation between intended difficulty and empirical failure rate

title: Choosing the Adaptation Locus in Multimodal Robot Policies
current_belief: Multimodal models contain encoders, connectors, and language backbones with different failure modes, so treating adaptation as one undifferentiated parameter update may be inefficient or brittle.
proposed_challenge: Compare encoder-only, connector-only, backbone-only, and sparse hybrid adaptation under matched parameter and compute budgets.
scientific_question: Which adaptation locus best improves a new embodied capability while preserving pretrained cross-modal grounding?

reasoning_summary: The study makes adaptation-locus choice an empirical selection problem with retention constraints.
expected_contribution_type: matched adaptation study and decision guide
cheap_falsifier: Fine-tune each locus on one compact grounding task; reject if all loci yield indistinguishable success, retention, and cost.
main_risk: Results may be architecture-specific and fail to support a general selection rule.
proposed_data_source: Open multimodal robot-policy checkpoints and paired image-instruction-action datasets
target_variable: held-out grounding retention at matched task success

title: Fine-Tune, Retrieve, or Combine for Embodied Knowledge?
current_belief: Fine-tuning and retrieval solve different adaptation problems, and the right architecture may depend on knowledge volatility, latency, and fail-closed behavior.
proposed_challenge: Build an auditable decision matrix for robot instructions that separates stable procedural skills from changing environment facts.

reasoning_summary: The candidate transfers a measured architecture-selection framework to embodied knowledge while preserving explicit fail-closed and interference tests.
cheap_falsifier: Create a small simulator set with stable skills and time-varying object facts; stop if the three architectures show no interaction with volatility.
main_risk: A small benchmark may encode the expected architecture ordering by construction.
proposed_data_source: Embodied instruction tasks with controlled updates to maps, object locations, and procedural rules
target_variable: task success by knowledge volatility class and architecture

title: Adversarial Detection Tokens for Robot Vision Transformers
current_belief: A dedicated detection token may identify adversarial inputs to vision transformers, but robot safety depends on detecting physically realizable and temporally persistent attacks.
proposed_challenge: Evaluate one-token adversarial detection inside a perception-control loop under digital and physical-style perturbations.

cheap_falsifier: Add a token to a small ViT controller under patch attacks; reject if attack scores cannot separate clean and attacked observations above a simple entropy baseline.

proposed_data_source: Vision-based driving or manipulation simulation with digital patches and viewpoint variation
target_variable: unsafe-action reduction at fixed clean performance

title: Training-Only Language Supervision Under Causal Reasoning Ablations
current_belief: Training-only language supervision can inject a staged perception-to-planning reasoning chain without autoregressive inference, but it is unclear which stages cause control gains.
proposed_challenge: Intervene on supervision stages and answer quality while keeping the visual-control architecture and inference cost fixed.

current_belief: Weakly supervised temporal localization can exploit knowledge selection, but confidence may be poorly calibrated on unseen viewpoints and skill compositions.

title: Procedural Invariance Tests for Robot Preference Elicitation
current_belief: Choice estimates can change with elicitation procedure, and open-ended formats may trade realism for flexibility and hypothetical bias.

target_variable: cross-procedure preference-ranking consistency

title: Calibration-Aware Abstention for Subjective Robot-Language Safety Labels
current_belief: Subjective harm labels contain annotator disagreement, yet training pipelines often collapse them to a single label and ignore uncertainty.

title: Natural-Attack Stress Tests for Embodied Infrastructure Networks
